calibration.chosen: V11, a per-market logistic recalibration. Unpenalized, fit on all of 2024-25 (71,922 props): logit p_fixed = a + b1*logit(p_over) + b2*log(line) + b3*(n1_mean-line)/sqrt(line) + b4*logit(p_over)*log(line) + b5*logit(p_over)^2. Fitted [a; b1..b5] by market: ast [-0.012; 0.339, -0.030, 0.268, -0.130, 0.073]; fg3m [0.329; 1.596, -0.147, -1.065, -0.296, 0.177]; pra [0.243; 0.598, -0.071, -0.361, -0.071, 0.040]; pts [0.084; 0.247, -0.053, 0.152, -0.144, 0.002]; reb [0.178; 1.101, -0.095, -0.642, -0.109, 0.193]. The logit term and the gap term are strongly collinear, so read the coefficients together, not one by one: their combined effect is a slope of about 0.3 on the model's logit plus an upward shift of the intercept. Selection rule: lowest out-of-fold log loss in leave-one-month-out CV on 2024-25 (7 month folds). V11 was also lowest under forward-chaining CV. I added V11 after the first CV pass, and it is counted in the 12. Its edge over V8 is +0.00002 (CI includes zero) and over V4 is +0.0003 (CI includes zero), so a rule that preferred the simplest model would have picked V4 instead. That difference is tiny next to the gap to the market. Only V11 was run on 2025-26.

distribution.chosen: N1 (nba-0.1, dispersions and minutes table unchanged) with three changes. (1) Per-stat rate factors fitted on 2024-25 props by mean matching: pts 1.0301, reb 1.0205, ast 1.0300, fg3m 1.0507. PRA picks these up through its components. (2) A shared lognormal multiplier on a player's pts/reb/ast rates in a game: log-sd 2.4, median 1 (log shift 0). It is shared, so PRA stays consistent with its parts. (3) fg3m gets its own multiplier: log-sd 1.0, log shift -0.05. The mixture is integrated on a log-multiplier grid from -3 to +3 in steps of 0.1, with tail mass folded into the end nodes. Selection was by leave-one-month-out log loss on 2024-25. The month-by-month picks were stable: shared width 2.0-2.4 with shift 0, and fg3m width 1.0-1.2 with shift -0.05. Caveat: a log-sd of 2.4 on the rates is not a realistic box-score distribution. At this width P(over) has become a smooth function of log(model median / line). It works as a recalibration through the distribution and should not replace N1's pmfs for anything else, such as CRPS or the app's distributions.

synthesis:
# Test of the fixes for the under bias and overconfidence, against real bookmaker lines

**Setup.**
- **NBA:** fitted on 2024-25 (71,922 props) and tested on a 2025-26 sample (18,753 props, 42 dates).
- **NFL:** fitted on weeks 1-11 of 2023 (6,025 props) and tested on weeks 12-22 (4,290 props).
- **Selection:** every variant was chosen by cross-validation on the fit data only. The chosen variant was then scored once on the test data.
- **Betting rule:** declared in advance. It needs at least 3 books, takes the side with the higher expected value (EV), and bets only when EV ≥ 0.02.
- **CIs:** 95% bootstrap intervals, resampling dates for NBA and weeks for NFL.

## 1. Do the fixes remove the under bias and the overconfidence?

**NBA: yes, all three fixes do. Test season 2025-26, actual over rate 0.4845.**

| Model | Mean P(over) | Calibration slope | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original N1 | 0.459 | 0.29 | ECE 0.064 |
| Calibration (V11) | 0.490 | 0.97 | ECE 0.0096, lower than the market's 0.0122 |
| Distribution fix | 0.490 | 1.01 | deciles within about 0.01 of actual |
| Market-anchored stack | 0.489 | 0.90 | about 95% market price |
| Market | 0.495 | 0.96 | |

ECE is the decile expected calibration error. A slope of 1 means no overconfidence.

- **Under bias:** gone in all three. They now lean slightly over, by about 0.5 points, as the market does.
- **Overconfidence:** almost all gone. Compared with the original N1, log loss improves by 0.017 to 0.019, and every CI excludes zero.
- **V11 is the only fix that repairs N1 itself.**
  - It uses no market price as an input.
  - It is the best calibrated of all on test.
  - Remaining flaws: the top decile is slightly overconfident (predicted 0.585, actual 0.568), and the slope varies by market from 0.81 (PRA) to 1.06 (3-pointers).
- **The distribution fix is a recalibration in disguise.** It only works because it widens player rates to a log-sd of 2.4, which is not a realistic box-score distribution. Realistic changes only moved fit log loss from 0.705 to about 0.700-0.703.
- **The stack borrows the market's price to get its calibration.** With a slope of 0.90 it is a little more overconfident than the market.

**NFL: the bias is fixed, but the overconfidence is only partly fixed.**
- Raw X1: mean 0.458 against an actual 0.496, slope 0.046. On the test weeks it has almost no information.
- X1 calibration: mean 0.493, slope 0.24, so still strongly overconfident.
- Ensemble of four models: mean 0.494, slope 0.18.
- Market blend: mean 0.495, slope 0.78. Its slope on its own deviation from the market is -0.42, so the X1 signal pointed the wrong way.
- All three improve log loss over raw X1 by 0.035 to 0.039, with CIs excluding zero. They cannot cure the overconfidence, because X1 has almost no signal to calibrate.

## 2. Does any fixed model beat the market on log loss out of sample?

**No.**

| Fix | Fixed | Market | Fixed minus market | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NBA calibration | 0.68793 | 0.68723 | +0.0007 | −0.0005 to +0.0019 |
| NBA distribution | 0.68858 | 0.68723 | +0.0014 | −0.0002 to +0.0030 |
| NBA stack | 0.68695 | 0.68723 | −0.0003 | −0.0006 to +0.0001 |
| NFL blend | 0.69039 | 0.68939 | +0.0010 | −0.00002 to +0.0020 |
| NFL calibration / ensemble | 0.6939 | 0.68939 | +0.0045 | both CIs exclude zero (worse than the market) |

- **The NBA stack is the only fix below the market at face value.**
  - It was also below the market in fit-season CV: −0.00022, CI −0.00039 to −0.00005.
  - On test its CI includes zero. Brier score shows the same: −0.00013, CI −0.00030 to +0.00003.
  - Even if this is real, it is the market price nudged about 5% toward N1 in three markets: assists, 3-pointers and rebounds. The N1 weight is effectively zero for points and PRA. It is not N1 beating the market.
- **The NBA calibration gap to the market shrank on test** (from +0.0027 on the fit season to +0.0007). That is mostly because the market itself scored worse on the test sample (0.6872 against 0.6856 on the fit season).

## 3. Does any betting rule make money out of sample?

None of the four fixes showed an edge with a CI above zero, so the verification step had nothing to check (its list is empty). No test ROI CI is above zero, at the best price or at BetMGM.

| Fix | Best price: bets, ROI [CI] | BetMGM: bets, ROI [CI] | Same rule, fit season out of fold |
|---|---|---|---|
| NBA calibration | 6,861, +1.1% [−1.2, +3.1] | 3,131, −1.4% [−5.1, +2.1] | −1.6% best / −3.1% BetMGM, both CIs below zero |
| NBA distribution | 8,343, +0.5% [−2.1, +2.8] | 3,698, −1.0% [−5.5, +3.3] | −2.6% / −3.8%, both CIs below zero |
| NBA stack | 1,162, +4.1% [−2.8, +10.4] | 263, +9.1% [−4.4, +22.5] | +1.1% [−1.6, +3.8] / +4.7% [−2.0, +11.0] |
| NFL blend | 537, −7.0% [−12.8, −2.4] | 64, −9.8% [−28.1, +13.5] | +3.1% best [−4.8, +11.1] |
| NFL calibration | 1,800, −3.3% [−6.4, −0.05] | 713, −4.6% [−9.5, +0.8] | −0.2% best |
| NFL ensemble | 1,732, −4.0% [−7.3, −0.04] | 692, −0.8% [−6.4, +5.5] | −0.7% best |
| Original NBA N1 (reference) | 11,619, −1.2% [−3.5, +1.2] | 7,415, −3.5% [−6.4, −0.7] | |

- **BetMGM** is the only regulated book tested on its own. No fix shows a profit there with a CI above zero.
  - NBA calibration and the distribution fix are negative at face value.
  - The stack's +9.1% comes from only 263 bets.
- **The positive best-price figures for NBA are not significant, and line shopping inflates them.**
  - The average best price taken was 2.15 to 2.16, against about 2.11 at BetMGM.
  - The market's own price, run through the same rule, bets 554 props at an average price of 2.28.
  - The best price across all books may not be available at your stake, so the best-price column overstates what is realistic.
- **NFL loses with every fix at the best price.** All three CIs are entirely below zero.
- **The NBA stack is the only rule that is positive at face value in both the fit season and the test, at both price sets.** That fits a small edge, but it also fits noise:
  - Four fixes were tested at two price sets, so one positive point estimate is likely by chance.
  - Telling a 2% edge apart from zero would take roughly 10,000 bets. This is my approximation, not something the test measured.

## 4. The single fix worth adopting in the live model

**For NBA, adopt V11, the per-market logistic recalibration of N1's P(over).**

Why V11:
- It uses no market price, so the model's view stays independent of the market.
- It is the variant that was scored once on test.
- It has the best test calibration of everything tested, including the market: slope 0.97, ECE 0.0096, mean 0.490 against an actual 0.4845.
- It cuts log loss by 0.0179 (CI −0.0238 to −0.0125), and Brier from 0.2549 to 0.2474.

It gives honest probabilities. It does not give an edge.

Caveats:
- V4 (two parameters per market) was within 0.0003 in CV, with a CI including zero, and is simpler. But V4 was never scored on test.
- Refit V11 each season.

**Do not adopt the distribution fix for the app's distributions.** At a log-sd of 2.4, its distributions are only valid for P(over) at a line.

**Use the stack only if the app should show a "best estimate"** rather than the model's own opinion. It is about 95% market and needs a live margin-free price from at least 3 books.

**For NFL, at most apply the global shrink:** p = expit(0.0081 + 0.1919·logit X1), so the app stops showing wildly overconfident numbers. On test it was still overconfident (slope 0.24) and clearly worse than the market. X1 carries no usable information beyond the market's margin-free price.

## 5. Plain conclusion for a bettor

The fixes work: the NBA model no longer leans to unders or overstates its confidence, and its probabilities are now about as well calibrated as the bookmaker's. Once the model is honest, though, it shows it knows nothing the market does not:
- No fixed model beat the market's margin-free price on the 2025-26 NBA sample or on late-2023 NFL.
- No betting rule made money out of sample with a CI above zero, at BetMGM or at the best price.
- The NFL bets lost money, with CIs entirely below zero.

Treat any model "edge" against these lines as zero. If you want to keep testing, the only candidate is to paper-track the NBA market-anchored stack, at BetMGM prices only, with the rule frozen.
